body:
This approach is better than the previous one since it accounts for tabs after the start of the line, but it's not completely correct either.
Tabs aren't always `indent_size`, they stop at tab boundaries even if there are already some characters before it.

It would have to iterate over the line and keep track of the tab alignment to get the proper column, if there are tabs after any non-tabs.

This approach is better than before where it only considered the start of the line, but it still isn't completely correct to get the visual column.
I don't think gdscript handled this correctly previously either.

Tabs aren't always 4 characters wide, they can be smaller for tab alignment.
So if there are tabs after the start of the string, this should iterate over the line to count the column and keep track of the alignment.
Edit: github didn't show me the previous version of this comment so I thought it didn't save and rewrote it, but now that one is back.

`count("\t")` isn't entirely correct because the tab width depends on the column it starts in. Perhaps we should add a helper method?

```c++
static int get_visual_column(const String &p_line, int p_raw_column) { ... }
```

It is not correct for the builtin editor, and there a different calculation is utilized. In this specific context it's correct since we do this:
```c++
String tab = String(" ").repeat(tab_size);
...
print_line(vformat("%04d %s", l, p_lines[l - 1]).replace("\t", tab));
```

It's a tool for debugging, it handles well formatted GDScript correctly. No need to reinvent the wheel here IMO
Tabs can appear in the middle of a line. You're right that an internal debugging tool isn't a high priority, but I'd still consider this case.
I guess I can fix the tab substitution as well. But I'd prefer not to touch unrelated code and fix this in a followup.
I'm not insisting on it. We can fix it later, it's not a blocker.
Alright then I'll do a followup for handling mid line tabs correctly.
